label: Explained absence: admitted reason, positive fixing, admissibility fixing
term: Explained absence: admitted reason, positive fixing, admissibility fixing
resolution: An absence at a root is 'explained' in sense 1 when some fact is admitted as a reason for the lack fact in the #755 arena (ADMITTED_EXPLICABILITY_ROLE_1, the sense of every PSR and inquiry bridge in the graph). It is explained in sense 3 when it is not an unexplained absence (a5452da9): the admissibility constraints, alone or with the bearer's profile, exclude the missing determination (case i or ii). This is the sense of 'no unexplained absence at roots' (9281317d). The sense-3 record defines its complement, so sense 3 is read as the negation of UnexplainedAbsence for a lacked determination. Sense 2 (positively fixed) is sense 3 or a carried exclusion. Sense 3 gives sense 2 by its first disjunct, and sense 2 gives sense 3 under the necessity direction of member grounding (89c988d9, carriedClosureNotUnexplained). Sense 1 gives neither: a bare negative clause, or any necessary truth under necessaryReasons, is an admitted reason for a necessary lack that no admissibility constraint fixes (InquiryClosure rival row). Passages between the senses are explicit premises listed in sense_bridges: the open bridge RootLackReasonsPositive (a8a43166) from 1 to 2; the necessity direction 89c988d9 from 2 to 3; the reason-essence thesis fedc67d8 from 1 to 3 together with carriage and 89c988d9; the factorization argument derives a8a43166 from fedc67d8, carriage and 89c988d9. See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section on inquiry and closure at the root.
